briefs.claim_en: 5G mobile towers are responsible for spreading the coronavirus, which caused an increase in COVID-19 cases in areas where 5G was installed.
briefs.brief_en: Multiple sources, including the UN agency International Telecommunication Union (ITU), the UK government, and the World Health Organization (WHO), state that there is no scientific evidence linking 5G mobile towers to the spread of the coronavirus. The ITU confirmed in April 2020 that 5G is not responsible for COVID-19, calling it a "hoax that has no technical basis." Experts explain that viruses cannot travel via radio waves or mobile networks, and 5G technology uses electromagnetic fields that cannot transfer particles like viruses. The UK government also noted that COVID-19 spread in countries without 5G. Fact-checking organizations like Full Fact, The Quint, AP News, Alt News, and FACTLY have rated claims connecting 5G to COVID-19, including the second wave in India and the EG.5 variant, as false. These conspiracy theories have led to arson attacks on 5G towers and harassment of telecom engineers in several countries.
